featured_reviews.name: Sarthak Choudhary
featured_reviews.review_text:
Gurudwara Shri Nanak Darbar is a place that truly radiates peace, devotion, and a strong sense of community. Located in Borivali, it offers a calm and spiritual escape from the fast-paced life of Mumbai.

The atmosphere inside the Gurudwara is incredibly serene, with soothing kirtans creating a deeply calming experience. Whether you visit regularly or for the first time, there’s a sense of warmth and welcome that makes you feel instantly at ease.

One of the most beautiful aspects is the langar seva, where everyone is served simple yet delicious food with humility and equality. The volunteers are kind and dedicated, ensuring everything is well-organized and that every visitor feels respected.

The premises are clean, well-maintained, and managed efficiently, allowing devotees to focus entirely on prayer and reflection. Overall, Gurudwara Shri Nanak Darbar is not just a place of worship, but a space that offers peace, positivity, and a sense of belonging.

featured_reviews.name: Rushikesh Bhoir
featured_reviews.review_text:
Attending my first Punjabi friend's wedding at a gurdwara was a beautiful experience. The entire atmosphere of the gurdwara, with its serene and welcoming ambiance, felt truly sacred and peaceful. As I entered, I was drawn to the calmness of the place, with the soft hum of prayers and the faint scent of incense filling the air. The sense of devotion was overwhelming yet calming, creating an indescribable sense of tranquility.

The wedding rituals themselves were simple yet deeply meaningful. The couple’s walk around the Guru Granth Sahib, the holy scripture, symbolized their spiritual commitment. I was fascinated by the importance of equality and humility in the Sikh faith; everyone sat together on the floor, heads covered, symbolizing unity and respect. The langar (community meal) served after the ceremony was a highlight, as it embodies the Sikh value of selfless service.

The experience left a lasting impression on me. The gurdwara’s traditions and values, like community, compassion, and devotion, were truly inspiring. It felt like a place of pure spirituality and peace, and it made me appreciate the warmth and inclusivity of Sikh culture even more.

For professional catering services, feel free to visit my profile." ~ chhaya caterers kandivali

featured_reviews.name: aruna mukerjee
featured_reviews.review_text:
I wouldn't even give one star but since i have to make others aware about the scammers here, i am doing so.

On the pretext of being a religious place, the representative of this Gurudwara functions hand-in-glove with valet parking organisations. On the occasion of Guru Nanak Jayanti, we visited in the evening and promptly handed over our car keys to the valet person. After more than 35 minutes of waiting, a threat to contact the police and a useless Gurudwara representative who did nothing, we were handed over our car without even an apology. Our car when we checked, had been running for 35 minutes and 10 kms with the AC running on 19 degrees. All this while, our old parents waited on the footpath while the valet guy chilled in our car and the Gurudwara representative was utterly useless and paid no attention to us or the urged the valets to do the right thing despite multiple requests.

It is such a shame that such a sacred place is associated with individuals who are focussed on scamming people. Next time, no matter what, don't hand over your car keys to any valet service here or any person from the Gurudwara.

I would also advice people to think twice before they even make any donations to this place, since this may just be the tip of the iceberg.

featured_reviews.name: Suryaprakash Barnwal
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had the privilege of visiting Sri Guru Nanak Darbar in Mira Road East on the occasion of Baisakhi, and it was truly a soul-stirring experience. The entire gurdwara was beautifully decorated, creating a warm and festive atmosphere that instantly lifted my spirits.

From the moment I stepped in, there was a sense of peace and spiritual calm. The kirtan was deeply moving, and the energy of the sangat coming together in celebration of such a significant day in Sikh history was heartening. The Baisakhi celebrations were well-organized, with traditional hymns, prayers, and a sense of togetherness that reminded me of the true essence of community and seva.

The langar was served with immense love and humility – simple yet wholesome, just as it should be. I could see volunteers of all ages working selflessly, which added to the sense of unity and devotion.

Overall, the visit to Sri Guru Nanak Darbar on Baisakhi left a lasting impression on me. It’s a place where faith, peace, and community come together beautifully. I highly recommend visiting, especially during such auspicious occasions.

featured_reviews.name: Himanshu Jhunjhunwala
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Divine Place of Peace, Seva, and Compassion

Four Bungalows Gurudwara in Andheri West is truly one of the most peaceful and spiritual places in Mumbai. The atmosphere here is filled with positivity and calmness — every visit brings a sense of inner peace and gratitude.

What makes this Gurudwara even more special is its continuous Langar Seva, served twice daily, 365 days a year, feeding thousands of people selflessly. The management and volunteers work with so much dedication and humility — a true example of Guru Nanak Dev Ji’s teachings of Seva (selfless service) and Sarbat da Bhala (well-being of all).

Their recent initiative of adopting three flood-affected villages in Punjab and helping families with seeds, diesel, and essentials shows how deeply this Gurudwara believes in serving humanity beyond boundaries.

Truly a sacred place where peace meets purpose. Grateful to the entire Suri family and the management for keeping the spirit of Seva alive every single day.

featured_reviews.name: Surjeet Singh
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Divine and Soulful Experience at Gurudwara Shri Dashmesh Darbar

Visiting Gurudwara Shri Dashmesh Darbar was a truly spiritual and heartwarming experience. The moment I stepped inside, I was embraced by an atmosphere of peace, devotion, and selfless service.

The prayer hall is beautifully maintained, resonating with the soothing sounds of Gurbani Kirtan that fill the space with positivity and tranquility. The aura of the Gurudwara is incredibly uplifting, making it an ideal place for prayer, meditation, and inner reflection.

The langar (community kitchen) is another highlight—serving delicious, simple, and nourishing meals to all, regardless of caste, creed, or background. The sense of equality and service is truly inspiring, as the volunteers work with devotion and kindness, ensuring everyone feels welcomed and cared for.

What stands out most about Gurudwara Shri Dashmesh Darbar is its deep-rooted commitment to seva (selfless service) and community well-being. Whether it's through feeding the needy, organizing charitable initiatives, or simply providing a peaceful sanctuary for worshippers, this Gurudwara embodies the true spirit of Sikhism.

If you are in Mumbai and looking for a place to find spiritual solace, peace, and community warmth, I highly recommend visiting Gurudwara Shri Dashmesh Darbar. It is more than just a place of worship—it is a place of love, unity, and divine blessings. 🙏✨

featured_reviews.name: Kirtan Chavda
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visiting Gurudwara Sri Dashmesh Darbar is a truly peaceful and uplifting experience. The place welcomes everyone, regardless of background, and offers daily langar (free meals) that brings the community together. The positive vibes, the kindness of volunteers, and the sense of belonging make it a must-visit spot for anyone seeking comfort or spiritual calm.

Most active gurudwara I've visited.

featured_reviews.name: Rajveer Singh RV
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had the most incredible experience at Gurudwara Dashmesh Darbar in GTB Nagar, Mumbai! The moment I stepped inside, I was enveloped in a sense of tranquility and serenity that I've never felt before. The warm welcome and hospitality from the devotees and staff were heartwarming.

The atmosphere inside the Gurudwara was filled with devotion and spirituality, instantly making me feel at peace. The sacred hymns and prayers filled the air, creating an aura of positivity that's truly indescribable. It felt like a sanctuary for the soul.

The Langar (community kitchen) was a unique and humbling experience. The selfless service of the volunteers providing delicious meals to everyone, regardless of their background, left me feeling incredibly blessed and grateful.

Every aspect of Gurudwara Dashmesh Darbar exudes a sense of unity, love, and compassion. The teachings and principles followed here are truly inspiring. It's a place where people from all walks of life can come together and find solace.

If you're seeking guaranteed peace of mind and a feeling of being blessed, I wholeheartedly recommend visiting Gurudwara Dashmesh Darbar in GTB Nagar, Mumbai. It's an experience that will touch your heart and leave a lasting impact on your soul..

Celebrating 552nd GURPURAB
SAHIB SRI GURU NANAK DEV JI, after lockdown today we celebrate the Prakash Purab, due to pandemic no one was allowed to go to Gurdware only people staying there inside would do prayers. But Langer( food) was made daily was served twice afternoon & night in lockdown . Taking all safety precautions food packets were given my tailor told me as no work, due to lockdown he used have food here every day, near by people staying in slum would come,take langar packets auto wala today told me mam there no passenger people were not moving in out in lockdown,it was difficult, but we got food from Sikh Gurdware, they serve us with smile face we used stand in queue wearing mask . I said yes most of Gurdware in Mumbai served langar
Today felt happy after years we got to celebrate with Grace of God all program went smoothly. Some were wearing mask some removed when entered inside . But I took all safety measures wore mask, during the whole program,had Langar left.And prayed 🙏to babaji bless everyone is safe and we living normal life.

located in raoli camp near Gtb nagar railway station
A place where you can find complete Peace..!!

featured_reviews.name: indu swrup2016
featured_reviews.review_text:
First time I visited .room no 8 very dirty  .
Washroom is full with garbage and urinal.i compain to authorities but they don't reply they only talking about charges or money. . very bad experience in Mumbai . Gurudwara is clean  .vaheguru management ko room & washroom clean karne ki sadbudhi de

featured_reviews.name: Kamaljit SIngh
featured_reviews.review_text: Clean, Gurdwara Air conditioned, Facilities for Cancer patients families to room for few days,Aryurvedic medicine at very low affordable price from last so many years

featured_reviews.name: Kulwinder Singh
featured_reviews.review_text: waheguru g.. there is sheleter for cancer patient ..at low price  ...but booking is full.so ..if any want cancer room in emergency contact the person i.e jai bavani ladies garment store in front of this gurudwara.that person have information about hari om mandir trust...who give room but inform them almost 1 month before vist

featured_reviews.name: amarpreet singh
featured_reviews.review_text: Nice and peaceful place. Present at the corner of road with easy visibility and in close proximity from sion railway station if you are traveling through central line (slow local).

featured_reviews.name: G. S. (Gypsy_Soul)
featured_reviews.review_text:
Lodging and boarding facilities provided to cancer patients and family members.

Around fifteen families can be accommodated.

It is within ten km of the Tata memorial hospital.

featured_reviews.name: Meghna Bairagi
featured_reviews.review_text: I liked the place.But they should allow cancer patients from any hospital.The management should not judge patient's financial condition by their Hospital.I didn't liked that "Only Tata Patients is allowed to stay".

featured_reviews.name: Murthy Brahmandam
featured_reviews.review_text: They provide accommodation at reasonable prices for certified cancer patients who come for treatment in Mumbai.

Sikhism is a true world religion. Their langar serves the whole world without any discrimination. We need more such true religious people who serve humanity considering all as their brothers and sisters.
Blessings to you gurudwara. Thank you
